ambiguities.text: The system call 'does not count against the block's gas limit'
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the system call gas is entirely separate from block gas accounting, but normal EVM rules (like SSTORE costs) still apply within the call.

ambiguities.text: HISTORY_SERVE_WINDOW is 8,191 blocks, but the reason for this specific number is not explained
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 8,191 is chosen as a prime number to ensure good hash distribution in the ring buffer and avoid aliasing patterns.

ambiguities.text: Behavior when SYSTEM_ADDRESS already has a balance is not specified
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume SYSTEM_ADDRESS is a reserved address that cannot normally receive ETH and any existing balance is irrelevant to the system call.

implicit_assumptions.description: The SYSTEM_ADDRESS (0xff..fe) cannot be controlled by any external entity
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If SYSTEM_ADDRESS could be controlled, attacker could write arbitrary hashes, breaking the chain's integrity
Hash collisions could allow attackers to substitute blocks or confuse contracts relying on hash verification

implicit_assumptions.description: All clients implement the system call at exactly the same point in block processing
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Inconsistent implementation could cause consensus failures between clients

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot manipulate block numbers to access hashes outside the intended window
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Could allow unauthorized access to stale or invalid hash data

implicit_assumptions.description: The ring buffer will be fully populated after 8,191 blocks post-activation
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Early blocks after activation may have undefined slots that could return zero or revert unpredictably
